name: Electric instead of gas-pneumatic controllers
applications: methane reduction at wellsites and compressor stations
principle: Gas-driven pneumatic controllers vent methane to operate valves; replacing them with instrument air or electric controllers removes that venting. EPA Natural Gas STAR reports gas pneumatic devices vented about 51 Bcf/yr in production (2006) and a conversion typically costs $45,000 to $75,000 with payback in months at $7/Mcf.

process_steps.name: Install instrument air or electric controllers

key_equipment: solar and battery power at remote sites

performance.metric: gas vented by pneumatic controllers in US production

source.note: US EPA Natural Gas STAR, Convert gas pneumatic controls to instrument air (lessons learned, 2006 data and dollars)

performance.metric: methane emission rate per pneumatic controller
performance.basis: Measured over 72 devices: high-bleed 19.25 scf/h (n=8), low-bleed 0.68 scf/h (n=19), all controllers 4.98 scf/h. Electric controllers vent nothing by design.

source.note: Luck et al., pneumatic controller emissions (ES&T Letters 2019), read 2026-11-17

notes: Process provenance: Compares replacement paths for natural-gas pneumatic controllers - instrument air (electric-driven compressor and dryers, clean/dry air piped to existing devices), liquid nitrogen (pressurised vessel plus regulators, 30-60 day refills), and electric actuators (retrofit, power/solar supply, cabling, remote monitoring).
